body:
Founder real-time, after repeated correct pushback that earlier fixes (fast-forward log flood, save-freq) hadn't actually solved the problem: reproduced the EXACT failure locally for the first time this session by matching the real training config exactly instead of an isolated single-client test -- real --save-freq, real --registry-url push to https://okemily.com, --heuristic-opponents 1, the actual real TRAINING_GROUND level. This hit the real 'TimeoutError: no live respawn snapshot within timeout' locally. Root cause, found by dumping raw packet bytes rather than continuing to guess: protocol.h's NetPlayer struct grew from 84 to 88 bytes when anim_override (S470) was added -- the exact same class of bug this codebase has already hit and fixed TWICE before (S459-44: 18->64/68, S459-69: 68/72->84), each time because a hand-maintained wire-format mirror wasn't updated when the real compiled C struct grew. This time it recurred in BOTH real mirrors simultaneously: rl_env_packet.py's own Python ctypes NetPlayer class (used by every RL Python script -- training, eval, the frozen-policy self-play bot) AND apps2/emily-bot/snapshot.go's own netPlayerSize constant (the real Go heuristic-bot binary, used both by SHANKPIT-RL training's own --heuristic-opponents flag AND as a real live QUEUE fallback bot outside training entirely -- a genuinely production-relevant bug, not training-only). With a stale, 4-byte-too-small stride, decode_snapshot correctly parses the FIRST entity in any multi-entity snapshot but reads every entity after it from the wrong offset -- garbage id/state/position. A real training client, which almost always connects as the SECOND participant (behind a heuristic bot or self-play opponent, exactly matching real production config), could therefore never find ITSELF among a snapshot's own entities -- _wait_for_alive_snapshot spun for its own full real timeout on literally every single reset(), regardless of the server's own health. A lone-client smoke test -- exactly what every earlier reproduction attempt this session used -- could never have caught this: with only one entity in the snapshot, there's no 'entity after the first' for the stale stride to misalign against. Fixed all three wire-format consumers: rl_env_packet.py's NetPlayer ctypes class (added the missing anim_override field + its own trailing padding, verified sizeof==88 via a real compiled C offsetof/sizeof probe, not guessed), its own self-checking assert (was silently checking the WRONG, stale expected size), test_rl_env_packet.py (same stale assertions, same fix), and emily-bot/snapshot.go's own netPlayerSize constant. Live-verified conclusively: reproduced the exact failure (real spawn + real --heuristic-opponents 1 bot + a real second connecting client) BEFORE this fix, confirmed it fails with the identical TimeoutError; the IDENTICAL scenario, same code, same ports, SUCCEEDS immediately after this fix, with zero other changes. go test ./apps2/emily-bot/... (13 tests) and python -m unittest discover (39 tests) both green. A full real production-config end-to-end run (real registry push, real save-freq) is running in the background as final confirmation. Commits: aa57dda (fix) + e0c7dec (changelog).

⚓ ☃
title: RL training: found and fixed the REAL bug -- NetPlayer wire struct grew to 88 bytes, both mirrors still at 84
